title: Symmetry of the Gaussian profile
statement: Let $U(\alpha)=\varphi(Q(\alpha))$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile, where $Q$ is the lower standard Gaussian quantile and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density. For every $a\in(0,1)$, $U(1-a)=U(a)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. For every $a\in(0,1)$, $I(1-a)=I(a)$.
